paper_title: DIY-MKG An LLM-Based Polyglot Language Learning System
caption: DIY-MKG reliably expands the vocabulary with low sensitivity to the language and the starting word. For each language, 10 opaque curves represent vocabulary sizes obtained from 10 different starting words, and one solid curve represents the average of the 10 curves. The standard deviations across languages and starting words are small, indicating fairness for all language learners. The diagonal gray line represents the upper-bound of vocabulary size, assuming all words in each iteration have not yet appeared in the vocabulary. While the real expansion rate is lower, the vocabulary does not saturate after 500 iterations. Therefore, DIY-MKG can reliably help the language learner to expand their vocabulary by consistently introducing new words.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between vocabulary size and the number of iterations for three languages: Spanish, Korean, and Japanese. The x-axis represents the number of iterations, with a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 500, and tick labels at intervals of 100. The y-axis represents vocabulary size, also with a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 5000, and tick labels at intervals of 1000. For each language, there are 10 opaque curves representing vocabulary sizes obtained from different starting words and one solid curve representing the average of these 10 curves. The Spanish vocabulary size starts at 0 and increases to approximately 4900 at 500 iterations on the upper-bound gray line. The average vocabulary size for Spanish increases from 0 to around 3400 at 500 iterations, with the 10 opaque curves closely clustered around it. Similarly, the average vocabulary size for Korean rises from 0 to about 3200 at 500 iterations, and for Japanese, it grows from 0 to roughly 3100 at 500 iterations, with both languages showing their respective 10 opaque curves tightly grouped around their average curves. The upper-bound gray line, representing the maximum possible vocabulary size, increases linearly from 0 to 5000 at 500 iterations. All average curves for the three languages exhibit a steadily increasing trend throughout the 500 iterations, with no signs of saturation.
